rules.statement: Protect a state-changing GET endpoint that cannot carry an anti-forgery header, such as RP-initiated logout, with a per-session random guard value that only the server hands out, and answer 400 and leave the session intact when the guard is missing or wrong.
rules.why: Logout is a top-level navigation that cannot carry the anti-forgery header, so without a guard any cross-site page could log the user out (logout CSRF).
rules.check: Look for GET logout or other state-changing GET handlers that end a session without checking a per-session secret parameter, or that still end the session when the check fails.

rules.statement: Compare secret values such as guards, tokens or MACs with `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals`, not with `==`, `string.Equals` or `SequenceEqual`.
rules.why: A constant-time comparison stops timing attacks from leaking the secret.
rules.check: Look for secret or guard values compared with ordinary equality operators or methods.

rules.statement: Reject a request with 400 when a security-relevant query or form parameter that should have one value (a guard, return URL or logout_token) appears more than once.
rules.why: Parameters that repeat are ambiguous and could be used to slip past validation.
rules.check: Look for handlers that read such parameters with first-value or joined-value access and never check that the count is exactly one, or at most one.

rules.statement: Redirect to a caller-supplied return URL only when it matches a configured allow-list, use a safe default such as `/` when it is absent, and answer 400 when it is not on the list.
rules.why: A return URL that is not checked makes the endpoint an open redirect.
rules.check: Look for redirects built from a request's returnUrl or similar parameter that is not checked against a configured allow-list.

rules.statement: Make logout idempotent: when no session exists, redirect to the return URL instead of failing.
rules.why: A second click or a stale tab should do no harm.
rules.check: Look for logout handlers that return an error when the session is already gone.

rules.statement: When ending a session, remove the local session record and delete its cookie first, using `CancellationToken.None`, before calling any remote service such as token revocation.
rules.why: If the client disconnects, it must not be able to leave the session behind by cancelling the request.
rules.check: Look for session removal that passes the request's cancellation token (HttpContext.RequestAborted), or that runs after remote calls that could fail or be cancelled.

rules.statement: Make best-effort cleanup calls during logout, such as RFC 7009 refresh-token revocation, with a bounded timeout, and log any failure (cancellation included) without failing the logout.
rules.why: The user asked to leave and the local session is already gone; the refresh token expires at the provider anyway.
rules.check: Look for revocation calls with no timeout, or whose exceptions (including OperationCanceledException) propagate and fail the logout.

rules.statement: In a back-channel logout receiver, find the affected sessions through `sid`/`sub` indexes rather than by scanning the store, and before ending each candidate check that its issuer, and its `sid` when the token has one, match the logout token.
rules.why: Scanning does not scale and needs a store that can list keys, and checking each candidate keeps a token from ending sessions it does not name.
rules.check: Look for store enumeration or key scans in logout handling, or for indexed candidates that are ended without checking issuer and sid.

rules.statement: Require a `sid` claim in back-channel logout tokens by default (matching `backchannel_logout_session_required=true`), and accept `sub`-only tokens only when an explicit option turns this off.
rules.why: Otherwise ending one provider session ends every session the user has at the relying party.
rules.check: Look for logout-token handling that accepts tokens without sid by default, or a session-required option whose default is false.

rules.statement: Record a logout token's `jti` as handled only after the sessions it names have ended, and do not record it when the receiver answers with an error.
rules.why: Recording it first would turn the provider's retry after a failure into a rejected replay.
rules.check: Look for jti/replay recording that happens before session removal, or that also runs on the error path.

rules.statement: Have a back-channel logout receiver answer 200 with `Cache-Control: no-store` on success, and 400 when the request or token is invalid, the provider's keys cannot be read, or a session cannot be ended.
rules.why: OpenID Connect Back-Channel Logout expects these responses, and a 400 lets the provider retry.
rules.check: Look for success responses without Cache-Control: no-store, or for failures that return 200 or 5xx instead of 400.
